**DonorDock and Network for Good (now Bonterra Guided Fundraising) are both nonprofit CRMs offering donor management, online giving pages, and email marketing, but DonorDock targets lean teams with simpler pricing and setup, while Network for Good suits larger nonprofits with higher fees and contracts.** [1][2][6]

### Key Feature Comparison
Both platforms support core functions like donor tracking, fundraising pages, email outreach, and integrations (e.g., Stripe, PayPal).[1][4] DonorDock adds text messaging, automations, project management (ActionBoard®), recurring gift tracking, and unlimited contacts, emphasizing ease for small-to-medium nonprofits.[4][5][6][7] Network for Good excels in quick check imports and yearly donor summaries but lacks robust outreach like calls or texts, with limits like 10,000 contacts on base plans.[1][2]

| Aspect              | DonorDock                          | Network for Good (Bonterra)              |
|---------------------|------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| **Pricing**        | $500/month flat; unlimited contacts; no contracts; 1% platform fee (+ Stripe processing) [1][5][6] | Starts ~$300/month (scales with contacts); 36-month contracts; 3% platform fee (+ processing); non-transparent [1][5][8] |
| **Setup & Usability** | Easiest setup; faster implementation; high adoption; self-guided imports [1][6][7] | User-friendly for imports but glitch reports and data loss issues [2][8] |
| **User Feedback**  | Praised for organization, reports, retention tracking, badges; best for small/medium orgs [2][7] | Easy imports but limited communication; good for basic tracking [2] |
| **Switching**      | Easy data export/import assistance; 90-day guarantee [1][3] | Part of Bonterra (acquired 2022); export steps available [1][3] |

### Strengths and Limitations
- **DonorDock**: All-in-one for growing teams; transparent costs; no contact limits; voted #1 easiest CRM.[1][6][7] Ideal if scaling without fee spikes.
- **Network for Good**: Established (since 2001); strong for large orgs and DAF processing.[3][8] Drawbacks include hidden pricing, bugs, and higher fees.[1][8]
Review sites like G2 and TrustRadius favor DonorDock for value and usability in smaller nonprofits.[2][7] Choose based on team size: DonorDock for lean operations, Network for Good for established ones needing brand recognition.[1][6]
